osces.title: Aortic Stenosis - Severity Assessment and Surgical Referral

patient_scenario.chief_complaint: Syncopal episode while gardening this morning, with associated chest tightness lasting 10 minutes
patient_scenario.history_presenting_illness: Mrs Thompson experienced sudden loss of consciousness while bending over in her garden at 9am today. Preceding symptoms included 5 minutes of central chest tightness (7/10 severity, pressure-like quality) and light-headedness. Regained consciousness after 30 seconds with no post-ictal confusion. Has noticed increasing exertional dyspnoea over 6 months, now occurring after walking 50 metres on flat ground (previously could walk 500m). Experiences chest pressure when climbing stairs, relieved by rest within 2-3 minutes. Orthopnoea requiring 3 pillows, no PND. Mild ankle swelling by evening.

social_history.exercise: Limited by dyspnoea to household activities
social_history.occupation_detail: Retired 13 years ago, previously active in garden club

patient_scenario.family_history: Father died age 82 from heart failure, mother had rheumatic fever as child

examination_findings.cardiovascular: JVP 6cm above sternal angle. Apex beat sustained and laterally displaced to 6th intercostal space anterior axillary line. Palpable systolic thrill at right 2nd intercostal space. S1 normal, S2 soft with absent A2 component. Grade 4/6 harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur loudest at right 2nd intercostal space, radiating to both carotids. Carotid pulse parvus et tardus bilaterally. No diastolic murmur. Bilateral ankle oedema to mid-shin.
examination_findings.respiratory: Bibasal fine inspiratory crepitations to mid-zones bilaterally. No wheeze or pleural rub.
examination_findings.other_systems: Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly or ascites. No peripheral stigmata of endocarditis.

investigations.ecg: 12-lead ECG shows sinus rhythm rate 72bpm, PR interval 200ms, QRS 110ms with left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage criteria (SV1 + RV5 = 42mm) and strain pattern with ST depression 2mm and T wave inversion in leads V5-6, I and aVL
investigations.chest_xray: Cardiomegaly with cardiothoracic ratio 0.58, prominent ascending aorta with calcification visible, upper lobe blood diversion and Kerley B lines at both bases consistent with mild pulmonary venous congestion
investigations.bloods: FBC: Hb 118 g/L, WCC 7.2 x10^9/L, Plt 245 x10^9/L. UEC: Na 138 mmol/L, K 4.2 mmol/L, Cr 95 μmol/L, eGFR 58 mL/min/1.73m². LFT normal. Troponin I 45 ng/L (normal <26). BNP 580 pg/mL (normal <100)
investigations.echocardiogram: Severe aortic stenosis with peak velocity 4.8 m/s, mean gradient 58 mmHg, calculated valve area 0.7 cm². Bicuspid aortic valve with heavy calcification. LV ejection fraction 48% with concentric LV hypertrophy (septal thickness 14mm, posterior wall 13mm). Mild mitral regurgitation. LA dilated at 45mm. PASP 45mmHg. No vegetation seen.
investigations.other: Coronary angiography shows 30% stenosis LAD, 20% RCA, no flow-limiting disease

immediate: Frusemide 40mg IV stat - PBS code 2622B
Continuous cardiac monitoring and hourly observations
Fluid restriction to 1.5L/day
Daily weight monitoring
short_term: Urgent cardiothoracic surgical referral for aortic valve replacement assessment
Heart team discussion for SAVR vs TAVI given age and comorbidities
Dental review and clearance pre-operatively
Coronary angiography if not recently performed
long_term: Aortic valve replacement (surgical or transcatheter based on heart team assessment)
Endocarditis prophylaxis not routinely recommended per current guidelines
Cardiac rehabilitation post-procedure
Annual echo surveillance if conservative management chosen
discharge_planning: Discharge once euvolaemic and surgical plan established
Avoid vigorous exertion pending valve replacement

marking_criteria.item: Recognises classical triad of severe AS (syncope, angina, dyspnoea)
Performs correct auscultation at right 2nd intercostal space
Identifies radiation of murmur to carotids
Checks for slow-rising carotid pulse (parvus et tardus)
Correctly grades murmur intensity and character
Orders appropriate investigations including echo and ECG
Interprets echo findings correctly (valve area <1.0cm² = severe)
Recognises indication for urgent valve replacement
Appropriately refers to cardiothoracic surgery
Discusses SAVR vs TAVI options based on patient factors
Initiates diuretic therapy for heart failure
Provides appropriate activity restriction advice

learning_objectives: Recognise clinical features of severe symptomatic aortic stenosis per CSANZ guidelines
Perform focused cardiovascular examination for valvular heart disease
Interpret echocardiographic severity criteria for aortic stenosis
Apply appropriate indications for aortic valve replacement per eTG Cardiovascular
references: CSANZ Position Statement on Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation 2023
National Heart Foundation - Management of Valvular Heart Disease Guidelines

osces.title: Mitral Regurgitation - Acute vs Chronic Differentiation

patient_scenario.chief_complaint: Sudden onset severe shortness of breath and pink frothy sputum since 3am this morning
patient_scenario.history_presenting_illness: Mr Chen woke at 3am with severe dyspnoea (10/10 severity), unable to lie flat, coughing up pink frothy sputum. Associated with severe retrosternal chest pain (8/10, crushing quality) starting 2 hours prior. Pain radiating to left arm and jaw. Diaphoresis and nausea present. Had inferior STEMI 5 days ago treated with primary PCI to RCA with drug-eluting stent. Was recovering well until this morning. Now extremely breathless at rest, orthopnoeic, using accessory muscles. No fever or productive cough prior to this episode.
past_medical_history: Inferior STEMI 5 days ago - RCA occlusion treated with PCI

social_history.smoking: Ex-smoker, quit 5 years ago, 30 pack-year history
social_history.exercise: Previously walked 30 minutes daily, inactive since MI
social_history.occupation_detail: Works from home, high stress job with long hours

patient_scenario.family_history: Father died of MI age 58, mother has AF

vital_signs.oxygen_saturation: 88% on room air, 92% on 15L/min via non-rebreather mask

examination_findings.cardiovascular: JVP elevated to angle of jaw when sitting upright. Apex beat displaced to 6th intercostal space anterior axillary line, hyperdynamic. S1 soft, S2 normal with loud P2, S3 gallop present. Grade 4/6 holosystolic murmur at apex radiating to axilla and back, no thrill. Bilateral pitting oedema to knees. Cool peripheries with capillary refill 4 seconds.
examination_findings.respiratory: Using accessory muscles, unable to speak in full sentences. Widespread coarse crepitations to apex bilaterally with wheeze. Pink frothy sputum visible.
examination_findings.other_systems: Abdomen distended with tender hepatomegaly 4cm below costal margin. No ascites.

investigations.ecg: Sinus tachycardia 115bpm, Q waves in II, III, aVF from recent inferior MI, new ST elevation 1mm in V5-6 with reciprocal depression in V1-3
investigations.chest_xray: Bilateral alveolar infiltrates in bat-wing distribution, Kerley B lines, enlarged cardiac silhouette CTR 0.62, bilateral pleural effusions, upper lobe blood diversion consistent with acute pulmonary oedema
investigations.bloods: FBC: Hb 132 g/L, WCC 14.2 x10^9/L, Plt 189 x10^9/L. UEC: Na 134 mmol/L, K 4.8 mmol/L, Cr 145 μmol/L, eGFR 45 mL/min/1.73m². High-sensitivity troponin I 8500 ng/L (normal <26), rising from 250 ng/L on admission 5 days ago. BNP 2400 pg/mL. ABG on 15L O2: pH 7.32, pO2 72mmHg, pCO2 32mmHg, HCO3 18mmol/L, lactate 4.2mmol/L
investigations.echocardiogram: Severe mitral regurgitation with flail posterior leaflet due to complete rupture of posteromedial papillary muscle. Eccentric jet directed anteriorly. EROA 0.65cm², regurgitant volume 85mL. Normal LV size (LVEDD 52mm) with hyperdynamic function (EF 65%). Inferior wall akinesis. Moderate pulmonary hypertension with PASP 55mmHg. No LA or LV thrombus.
investigations.other: Urgent coronary angiography shows patent RCA stent, no new culprit lesion, confirmed papillary muscle rupture on ventriculography

immediate: GTN infusion 5-200 mcg/min titrated to BP - PBS code 1735N
Frusemide 80mg IV stat then 20mg/hr infusion - PBS code 2622B
Morphine 2.5-5mg IV for dyspnoea and anxiety - PBS code 2696N
CPAP/BiPAP if not improving with medical therapy
Intra-aortic balloon pump insertion for afterload reduction
Emergency cardiothoracic surgical consultation
short_term: Emergency mitral valve repair or replacement within 6 hours
ICU admission post-operatively
Inotropic support as required
Mechanical ventilation until stable
long_term: Cardiac rehabilitation program
Lifelong anticoagulation if mechanical valve
Regular echo surveillance
Heart failure management with ACE inhibitor and beta-blocker optimisation
discharge_planning: ICU/HDU care initially, ward when stable
Warfarin if mechanical valve with INR target 2.5-3.5
Continue dual antiplatelet therapy for recent stent

marking_criteria.item: Recognises acute severe MR post-MI (papillary muscle rupture)
Differentiates from chronic MR by normal LV size on echo
Identifies holosystolic murmur at apex radiating to axilla
Recognises signs of acute pulmonary oedema
Orders urgent echo to confirm diagnosis
Initiates vasodilator therapy (GTN) for afterload reduction
Administers IV diuretics for pulmonary oedema
Recognises need for emergency surgery
Arranges IABP for haemodynamic support
Provides appropriate respiratory support (CPAP/BiPAP)
Manages cardiogenic shock appropriately
Coordinates with cardiothoracic team urgently

learning_objectives: Differentiate acute from chronic mitral regurgitation using clinical and echo findings
Recognise mechanical complications of myocardial infarction
Manage acute pulmonary oedema and cardiogenic shock per eTG guidelines
Understand indications for emergency cardiac surgery in acute MR
references: eTG - Cardiovascular: Acute heart failure management
CSANZ Guidelines for the Management of Acute Coronary Syndromes 2023
National Heart Foundation - Mechanical Complications of MI

osces.title: Infective Endocarditis - Modified Duke Criteria Application

patient_scenario.chief_complaint: Fever for 3 weeks with night sweats and new shortness of breath
patient_scenario.history_presenting_illness: Ms O'Brien presents with 3 weeks of intermittent fever (up to 39.5°C), drenching night sweats requiring change of clothes, and 5kg unintentional weight loss. Progressive exertional dyspnoea over past week, now SOB after one flight of stairs. Developed painful red spots on fingers 3 days ago. Noticed small red spots under fingernails yesterday. Had mitral valve prolapse diagnosed age 20. Dental extraction 6 weeks ago for infected molar, given amoxycillin for 5 days. No chest pain, palpitations, or syncope. Generalised arthralgia and myalgia. Poor appetite, early satiety.
past_medical_history: Mitral valve prolapse with mild regurgitation diagnosed 2012

social_history.exercise: Usually runs 5km three times weekly, unable last 3 weeks
social_history.occupation_detail: Daily exposure to oral bacteria, excellent dental hygiene

patient_scenario.family_history: Mother has rheumatic heart disease, father healthy

examination_findings.cardiovascular: JVP 4cm above sternal angle. Apex beat 5th intercostal space mid-clavicular line. Grade 3/6 pansystolic murmur at apex radiating to axilla (previously documented as 2/6). New early diastolic murmur grade 2/6 at left sternal edge. Peripheral pulses bounding. No clinical signs of heart failure.
examination_findings.respiratory: Bibasal fine crepitations. No wheeze or pleural rub.
examination_findings.other_systems: Osler nodes on 2nd and 3rd finger pads bilaterally (tender, raised, red). Janeway lesions on thenar eminence (non-tender, macular). Splinter haemorrhages under 3 fingernails. Roth spots on fundoscopy. Splenomegaly 2cm below costal margin. No focal neurology.

investigations.ecg: Sinus tachycardia 105bpm, normal axis, no conduction abnormalities, no ischaemic changes
investigations.chest_xray: Normal heart size, clear lung fields, no consolidation or effusion
investigations.bloods: FBC: Hb 102 g/L (normocytic), WCC 15.8 x10^9/L (neutrophilia 82%), Plt 142 x10^9/L. ESR 95 mm/hr, CRP 156 mg/L. UEC: Na 136 mmol/L, K 3.9 mmol/L, Cr 78 μmol/L, eGFR 82 mL/min/1.73m². LFT: mild transaminitis ALT 65 U/L. Rheumatoid factor positive 45 IU/mL. Urinalysis: microscopic haematuria, proteinuria 2+, no casts
investigations.echocardiogram: Mobile vegetation 12mm x 8mm on anterior mitral valve leaflet. Moderate to severe mitral regurgitation (increased from mild). Mild aortic regurgitation (new). Normal LV size and function (EF 60%). No abscess or fistula. PASP 35mmHg.
investigations.other: Blood cultures (3 sets before antibiotics): All 6 bottles positive for Streptococcus viridans, sensitive to benzylpenicillin (MIC 0.06 mg/L) and gentamicin

immediate: Take 3 sets of blood cultures from different sites before antibiotics
Start empirical therapy: Benzylpenicillin 1.8g IV 4-hourly - PBS code 8137L
Plus Gentamicin 1mg/kg IV BD (adjust for levels) - PBS code 2314R
Continuous cardiac monitoring
Daily examination for new murmurs or embolic phenomena
short_term: Continue IV antibiotics for 4 weeks (native valve endocarditis)
Monitor gentamicin levels (trough <1mg/L, peak 3-5mg/L)
Weekly inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR)
Weekly echo to monitor vegetation size and valve function
Cardiothoracic surgical consultation for valve assessment
long_term: Complete 4-week IV antibiotic course
Consider surgery if vegetation >10mm with embolic event or severe valve dysfunction
Dental review and treatment of any oral infection source
Echo at completion of therapy and 3 months later
Lifelong endocarditis prophylaxis education
discharge_planning: Hospital-in-the-home for IV antibiotics if stable
Education on signs of complications (emboli, heart failure)
Infectious diseases and cardiology follow-up in 2 weeks

marking_criteria.item: Takes 3 sets of blood cultures before antibiotics
Correctly applies Modified Duke Criteria
Identifies major criteria (positive blood cultures, vegetation on echo)
Identifies minor criteria (fever, predisposition, vascular/immunologic phenomena)
Recognises Osler nodes and Janeway lesions
Starts appropriate empirical antibiotics per eTG
Orders gentamicin levels and adjusts dosing
Monitors for complications with serial echo
Considers surgical indications (vegetation size, emboli)
Plans 4-week IV antibiotic course for native valve
Arranges appropriate follow-up and monitoring

learning_objectives: Apply Modified Duke Criteria for diagnosis of infective endocarditis
Recognise peripheral stigmata of endocarditis (Osler nodes, Janeway lesions, splinter haemorrhages)
Select appropriate empirical antibiotics according to eTG Antibiotic guidelines
Understand indications for surgical intervention in endocarditis per CSANZ guidelines
references: CSANZ Position Statement on Infective Endocarditis 2021
National Heart Foundation - Prevention of Endocarditis Guidelines

osces.title: Restrictive Cardiomyopathy vs Constrictive Pericarditis Differentiation

patient_scenario.chief_complaint: Progressive abdominal swelling and leg oedema over 6 months
patient_scenario.history_presenting_illness: Mr Papadopoulos presents with 6 months of progressive abdominal distension, now requiring paracentesis monthly (4-5L removed each time). Bilateral leg oedema to thighs, scrotal oedema developed 2 months ago. Exertional dyspnoea limiting him to 20 metres on flat ground. Orthopnoea requiring 4 pillows. Early satiety, 10kg weight gain despite poor appetite. No chest pain or palpitations. Had tuberculosis age 25 while working in PNG, treated with 6 months therapy. Recently returned from 2-year construction project in Darwin. Noticed prominent neck veins that worsen with inspiration.
past_medical_history: Chronic back pain from work injury 2015

social_history.alcohol: Previous heavy drinker (60 standard drinks/week), abstinent 5 years
social_history.exercise: Previously very active at work, now limited by symptoms
social_history.occupation_detail: Heavy manual labour, dust exposure, worked in tropical areas

patient_scenario.family_history: No cardiac disease, father had cirrhosis

examination_findings.cardiovascular: JVP elevated to ear lobe when sitting at 45 degrees with prominent x and y descents. Kussmaul's sign positive (JVP rises with inspiration). No apex beat palpable. Heart sounds distant, pericardial knock present (high-pitched sound after S2). No murmurs. Peripheral oedema to sacrum.
examination_findings.respiratory: Reduced air entry bibasally with dullness to percussion (bilateral pleural effusions). No crepitations.
examination_findings.other_systems: Abdomen grossly distended with shifting dullness (ascites). Hepatomegaly 6cm below costal margin, pulsatile. Splenomegaly 3cm. Prominent abdominal wall veins.

investigations.ecg: Low voltage QRS complexes (<5mm in limb leads), widespread non-specific T wave changes, no electrical alternans
investigations.chest_xray: Normal heart size, pericardial calcification visible along left heart border and diaphragmatic surface (rim-like), bilateral pleural effusions, clear lung fields
investigations.bloods: FBC: Hb 108 g/L, WCC 6.8 x10^9/L, Plt 165 x10^9/L. UEC: Na 132 mmol/L, K 3.6 mmol/L, Cr 125 μmol/L, eGFR 52 mL/min/1.73m². LFT: Albumin 28 g/L, bilirubin 45 μmol/L (conjugated), ALT 85 U/L, ALP 180 U/L, INR 1.4. BNP 250 pg/mL (lower than expected for degree of symptoms)
investigations.echocardiogram: Normal LV size and systolic function (EF 55%). Thickened, echogenic pericardium with respiratory septal shift (ventricular interdependence). Inferior vena cava dilated (25mm) with <50% respiratory variation. Tissue Doppler: Annulus reversus (septal e' > lateral e' = 12 vs 8 cm/s). Hepatic vein flow shows prominent diastolic flow reversal with expiration.
investigations.other: Cardiac catheterisation: Equalisation of diastolic pressures (RA = RV = PA diastolic = PCWP = 18mmHg). Ventricular pressure tracings show square root sign (dip-and-plateau pattern). Discordant RV and LV systolic pressures with respiration. CT chest: Pericardial thickness 8mm (normal <4mm) with extensive calcification

immediate: Cautious diuresis - Frusemide 40mg IV BD (monitor for hypotension) - PBS code 2622B
Fluid restriction to 1L/day
Salt restriction <2g/day
Daily weights and fluid balance
Consider therapeutic paracentesis if tense ascites
short_term: Cardiac MRI to further assess pericardial thickness and inflammation
Cardiothoracic surgical consultation for pericardiectomy evaluation
TB testing (Quantiferon Gold) to exclude active tuberculosis
Trial of anti-inflammatory therapy if inflammatory markers elevated (colchicine, prednisolone)
long_term: Pericardiectomy if confirmed constrictive pericarditis with ongoing symptoms
High-risk surgery with 5-10% mortality in experienced centres
Post-operative cardiac rehabilitation
Long-term follow-up for recurrence
discharge_planning: Patient education on fluid and salt restriction

marking_criteria.item: Recognises Kussmaul's sign (JVP rises with inspiration)
Identifies pericardial knock on auscultation
Notes pericardial calcification on chest X-ray
Orders appropriate imaging (echo with tissue Doppler)
Interprets annulus reversus correctly (septal e' > lateral e')
Recognises square root sign on cardiac catheterisation
Differentiates from restrictive cardiomyopathy using imaging
Considers TB as aetiology given history
Appropriately cautious with diuretics (preload dependent)
Refers for pericardiectomy consideration
Orders cardiac MRI for further assessment

learning_objectives: Differentiate constrictive pericarditis from restrictive cardiomyopathy using clinical and echo features
Recognise characteristic haemodynamic findings of constriction (equalisation of pressures, square root sign)
Understand role of tissue Doppler and annulus reversus in diagnosis
Apply appropriate management including surgical referral per eTG Cardiovascular
references: National Heart Foundation - Imaging in Constrictive Pericarditis

osces.title: Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy - Stress-Induced Cardiomyopathy Recognition

patient_scenario.chief_complaint: Severe chest pain following news of husband's sudden death 3 hours ago
patient_scenario.history_presenting_illness: Mrs Watson presents 3 hours after being informed of her husband's sudden death in a motor vehicle accident. Developed severe central chest pain (9/10 severity) immediately after receiving the news, described as heavy pressure sensation. Pain radiating to both arms and jaw. Associated dyspnoea, nausea, and diaphoresis. Pain persistent, not relieved by GTN spray given by paramedics. No previous cardiac symptoms. Has been under significant stress caring for husband with dementia over past 2 years. Post-menopausal for 18 years. Denies fever, cough, or recent illness.

social_history.exercise: Previously walked daily, reduced due to carer duties
social_history.occupation_detail: Retired 3 years ago after 40 years teaching, full-time carer for husband

patient_scenario.family_history: Mother died age 85 from stroke, father age 82 from pneumonia, no premature cardiac disease

examination_findings.cardiovascular: JVP 5cm above sternal angle. Apex beat 5th intercostal space mid-clavicular line. S1 and S2 normal, S3 gallop present. Grade 2/6 systolic murmur at apex. No peripheral oedema. Peripheral pulses intact.
examination_findings.other_systems: Emotionally distressed, tearful. Abdomen soft, non-tender. No focal neurological deficits.

investigations.ecg: Sinus rhythm 98bpm, ST elevation 2-3mm in V3-V6, I and aVL with reciprocal depression in III and aVF. QTc prolonged at 480ms. Deep T wave inversions developing in precordial leads.
investigations.chest_xray: Mild cardiomegaly CTR 0.52, pulmonary vascular congestion, no focal consolidation
investigations.bloods: FBC: Hb 128 g/L, WCC 11.2 x10^9/L, Plt 210 x10^9/L. UEC: Na 138 mmol/L, K 3.8 mmol/L, Cr 72 μmol/L, eGFR 75 mL/min/1.73m². High-sensitivity troponin I 450 ng/L (normal <26), rising to 890 ng/L at 3 hours. BNP 680 pg/mL. CK 180 U/L (normal <200)
investigations.echocardiogram: Characteristic apical ballooning with akinesis of apical and mid-ventricular segments, hyperkinesis of basal segments. LVEF 35%. No LV thrombus. Mild functional mitral regurgitation. No pericardial effusion. Right ventricle normal size and function.
investigations.other: Emergency coronary angiography: Normal coronary arteries with no significant stenosis, TIMI 3 flow in all vessels. Left ventriculography confirms apical ballooning pattern consistent with takotsubo cardiomyopathy.

immediate: Aspirin 300mg PO stat pending angiography - PBS code 1615Y
Metoprolol 25mg PO BD (cardioprotection) - PBS code 2012T
Heparin infusion until angiography excludes ACS - PBS code 1840Y
Continuous cardiac monitoring
Emotional support and counselling services
short_term: Continue beta-blocker (metoprolol 25-50mg BD)
Start ACE inhibitor (perindopril 2.5mg daily) - PBS code 8793X
Consider anticoagulation for 3 months if apical thrombus develops
Serial echo at 48 hours and 1 week to monitor recovery
Cardiac MRI if diagnosis uncertain
long_term: Continue ACE inhibitor and beta-blocker for 3-6 months
Echo at 3 months to confirm LV recovery (expected in >95%)
Psychological support and grief counselling
Stress management strategies
Education about benign prognosis with full recovery expected
discharge_planning: Cardiology follow-up in 2 weeks with repeat echo

marking_criteria.item: Identifies emotional trigger (husband's death) as precipitant
Recognises ST elevation mimicking acute MI
Orders urgent coronary angiography to exclude ACS
Identifies normal coronary arteries on angiography
Recognises characteristic apical ballooning on echo/ventriculography
Notes basal hyperkinesis with apical akinesis pattern
Initiates beta-blocker therapy
Starts ACE inhibitor for LV dysfunction
Considers anticoagulation if apical thrombus present
Plans serial echo to monitor recovery
Provides psychological support and counselling referral
Educates about good prognosis with expected full recovery

learning_objectives: Recognise takotsubo cardiomyopathy presentation following emotional stress
Differentiate from acute coronary syndrome using angiography findings
Identify characteristic apical ballooning pattern on echocardiography
Understand management is supportive with expected full recovery per eTG Cardiovascular
references: CSANZ Position Statement on Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy 2022
National Heart Foundation - Stress Cardiomyopathy Guidelines
